candidates.title: Referee model stops accepting outputs for good once one prove_output request's fixed audience has no new proof: later valid proofs, from newcomers or from audience members, are never heard
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua wait_for_outputs over game-transport.lua request_first_valid/dispatch_request/accept_scheduled_response/step_time)
candidates.role: Referee model (AUDIT.md component table: 'The PRT referee model in doc/recipes | Referee model')
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua wait_for_outputs (774-802); doc/recipes/game-transport.lua dispatch_request/register_event (669-687, 826-838: audience fixed from get_players() at request time), accept_scheduled_response (925-939: 'not future.audience[response.connection]' -> ignored), step_time (1108-1137: time advances only to supplied boundaries; a FOREVER wait whose prompt answers were all consumed supplies none), receive loop (586-597: unsolicited lines without the current request id are ignored)
candidates.description: wait_for_outputs accepts outputs one at a time: each iteration issues request_first_valid(EVERYONE, prove_output) and waits FOREVER; the next request is issued only after one output is accepted. The transport fixes a request's audience to the player connections that are live when it is issued (dispatch_request -> register_event/future.audience), and accept_scheduled_response ignores any response from a connection outside that audience. Each audience member effectively gets one answer per request: its prompt reply (or one scheduled reply) is included at block+1, after which its pending entry is 'true', no future block remains as a boundary, so the logical clock never advances again, no advance_time is sent, and a further reply has no channel (an unsolicited line without the outstanding request id is dropped by the reader). Hence, as soon as every member of the current request's audience has answered without a new valid proof (e.g. the honest player re-offers its already accepted last output, which the validator refuses as a duplicate index), the referee is frozen in that request forever: (a) a party that connects afterwards with a valid proof of another output of the settled state is never asked, and even if it pushes the proof under the future's id in an advance_time reply it is ignored as not in the audience; (b) an audience member that later has another valid proof cannot present it either. The same fixed-audience/one-shot pattern governs the prove_outputs_merkle_root request (FOREVER, audience = players live when the winner is known). A deployed referee (Dave/rollups Application.validateOutput) accepts a valid output proof from any sender at any time after settlement; the model reaches a state in which it refuses every later valid proof of an output the settled state commits to.
candidates.trigger: No adversary needed; it is the demo's normal end state. The honest player (prt.lua event_handler.prove_output) offers only the epoch's last output; after it is accepted, the next prove_output request gets the same index again, which the validator refuses (accepted_output_indices), and the model then stops listening. Any other output of the epoch (e.g. output 0 of the calculator epoch, or outputs the template already commits to) can then never be accepted by anyone. An adversary can also arrange it: being in the audience changes nothing, but any party not connected when the current request was issued is shut out permanently.
candidates.reachability: Reachable in the shipped demonstration (doc/README.md 'The player offered its last output, output 1'): after the first accepted output, the referee's next prove_output request is answered by the honest player with the same output and rejected; the referee then waits forever with no boundary. Experimentally reproduced at the transport level with the shipped game-transport.lua and game-test-server.lua (see evidence).
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion applies. The trigger is the referee model's own acceptance rule on valid output proofs of a settled, accepted state; THREAT_MODEL section 8 excludes 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)', and here the referee model is what violates A5. Not an application stall (the application is correctly designed; its outputs are committed by the settled state).

2. Role: referee model (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT referee model in doc/recipes | Referee model'). Section 3: 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' Counter-reading: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond, or only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support.' The facts that decide: the model is not crashed and not waiting on a silent party; it keeps running but refuses valid proofs presented by parties outside a frozen audience, which is a defect in what it accepts.

3. High/Medium cases: none of the High cases fits (not a verifier on unreachable states, not a cost factor). Under the support reading it is 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium' -> Medium, since in the role it stands in for (deployed referee) it would be Critical.

4. Critical: violates A5 at a reachable state: 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' After the first repeated offer, every further valid output proof is refused regardless of who presents it.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (referee-model defect in what it accepts, A5 converse); Medium under the reading that a referee-model liveness failure is 'only stalls the model' (support)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal's second half requires that the application can obtain every output the settled state commits to (A5 converse); a referee with this acceptance rule settles the right state but permanently refuses most of its outputs (vouchers/withdrawals), so a correctly designed application loses the outputs of the honestly settled epoch without any adversary action.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBREFSTATE/late-presenter.lua (lua5.4 with bugs/env.sh) using the shipped game-transport.lua and game-test-server.lua: player A (audience) answers a request_first_valid(EVERYONE) with a refused value; player B connects after the request with a valid answer and also pushes it under the future's id in each advance_time batch. Result: 'accepted=false time=19 B_asked=0 B_batches=2' (exit 1). Control (B connected before the request): 'accepted=true time=1 B_asked=1' (exit 0). The experiment uses a bounded wait only so it terminates; wait_for_outputs waits FOREVER, where after the prompt answers no boundary remains and B would not even receive advance_time.
candidates.test_idea: Run the prt.lua referee on the calculator epoch (or drive wait_for_outputs through game-test-server with a stub settled state): once the honest player's last output is accepted and its repeated offer refused, connect a new client that answers prove_output (or pushes in advance_time) with a valid proof of output 0 of the settled state; assert that the referee reports output 0 as accepted within a bounded number of dispatcher steps/blocks. Fails today (never accepted). Equivalent transport-level assertion: a request_first_valid(EVERYONE) future must accept a valid answer from a player that connected after the request.

candidates.title: Referee model binds a claim to the TCP connections that posted it: an honest operator that restarts (R4) can never again answer for its claim, which then loses by timeout
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua partition_claims/subscription_hash and every request addressed to claim holders; game-transport.lua subscriptions, accept_subscribers)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua partition_claims 230-258 (only place that subscribes holders, per response.connection), reveal_divergence 608-616, seal_divergence 638-646, emit_win_match_by_timeout 371-381, settle_uarch_state_hash 410-432, open_uarch_tournament 476-489; doc/recipes/game-transport.lua subscribe_connection 623-630 and accept_subscribers 900-917 (the only other subscription), get_subscribers 634-656, accept_scheduled_response 933 (audience check)
candidates.description: Holders of a claim are the connection objects whose claim response was accepted; subscriptions are never extended. Bisection, seal, timeout-win, uarch-claim admission and leaf proofs for a claim are requested only from, and accepted only from, those connections (audience check in accept_scheduled_response). An honest operator that stops and restarts, as R4 requires it to be able to ('After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'), comes back on a new connection: it is not a holder of its claim, cannot re-post it (claim collection is closed; a connection arriving after the phase close is not even subscribed to the initial state hash), and is not in the audience of any request about the claim. Its next on-turn deadline passes and the claim loses by timeout (or is eliminated), while the restarted operator acts within the claim's clock. Dave identifies a claim by its commitment and lets any sender advance, seal, win by timeout or prove (the manual itself says 'a claim does not belong to the player that posted it ... the sender does not matter'). Today the restart is masked by R3-VARREFMODEL-2 (the referee crashes on the disconnect); once that crash is fixed by dropping the dead connection, this becomes the outcome.
candidates.trigger: The honest player process stops (crash/kill) during an open match and restarts (e.g. from its stored epoch directory with prt.lua honest ... <epoch-directory>), reconnecting to the referee.
candidates.reachability: Reachable for any match with the honest claim on turn after a restart; requires the referee not to crash on the disconnect (currently it asserts, R3-VARREFMODEL-2). Closely related to R2-DFCLAIM-1 (dropped by triage: moves accepted only from posters); this candidate adds the concrete consequence under R4's restart obligation.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Restart is on the honest operator's path ('Restarting after a stop (O2)', section 2), not excluded. Not an A1-A8 violation by the deployment other than through the referee model itself.
2. Role: referee model; 'Which claim a timeout or an elimination decides is part of what it derives.' A defect in what it accepts is rated as if a deployed referee had it.
3. High/Medium: not a listed case. If triage reads it as only 'how long a claim may take to respond' it would be support (Medium at most).

4. Critical: violates A7 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock' and R4's restart clause, at a reachable state (any match after an honest restart).

5. Low: if the model's per-connection holder identity is accepted as a documented simplification (manual 10614: 'every player that posted one becomes a holder of it') and the restart is deemed outside the model's scope, Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (A7/R4 via the referee model); Medium or Low if read as a documented demo simplification or masked by R3-VARREFMODEL-2
candidates.threat_to_goal: If the honest claim cannot be defended after a restart, the honest claim is eliminated and a dishonest claim can win (completeness failure of the dispute as modeled).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: grep shows subscribe_connection is called only from accept_subscribers (initial hash, before phase close) and partition_claims (per accepted response connection). No experiment (a restart currently crashes the referee, R3-VARREFMODEL-2).
candidates.test_idea: With R3-VARREFMODEL-2 worked around in the test (or simulated by closing the honest connection with an announced 'done' and opening a new one), run the referee with the honest player and a quitter-like adversary that bisects; restart the honest player mid-match on a new connection; assert the honest claim wins (the restarted player can answer reveal/seal/prove requests for its claim).

not_covered: Dave clock carry-over (childReturnAllowance, pauseWinnerAt, winner expiry) versus the model's static clocks: compared only by reading; the manual lists 'no clock runs down', the uarch-result-at-once propagation and the leaf-race difference as simplifications, so no candidate.

Leaf-match timing: model accepts leaf proofs until the later deadline, Dave only before the earlier one and then a timeout win for the longer clock; documented simplification in the manual, not reported.
